protocolPicker.autoVerifyBody: After deployment, the app verifies from this machine whether the target TCP port is actually reachable from the public internet.
protocolPicker.comparisonCaption: VLESS Reality vs Hysteria 2 protocol comparison
protocolPicker.errorNodeNameTooLong: Node name must not exceed {{max}} characters
protocolPicker.errorPortRange: Listen port must be an integer between 1–65535
protocolPicker.errorSniInvalid: SNI must be a valid domain, e.g. www.microsoft.com
protocolPicker.hy2NoteBody: This protocol doesn't need SNI, but the cloud security group must allow the corresponding UDP port — otherwise clients can't connect at all.
protocolPicker.hysteria2Firewall: Must allow the UDP port in cloud firewall / security groups
protocolPicker.hysteria2Scenario: High throughput, weak or mobile networks
protocolPicker.hysteria2Subtitle: Geared toward high throughput and weak networks; configuration is more straightforward.
protocolPicker.namingCalloutBody: VPS names group machines and reuse login details; node names only describe this protocol instance. You can create multiple differently-named nodes under one VPS.
protocolPicker.nodeNameHint: This is the name clients see; it won't overwrite the VPS card name.
protocolPicker.nodeNamePlaceholder: e.g. Main VLESS line / Gaming Hysteria2
protocolPicker.portHintHy2: Prefer an unused UDP port between 10000 and 60000.
protocolPicker.portHintVless: For VLESS Reality, prefer 443; switch to another free TCP port if it's taken.
protocolPicker.sniHint: Only needed for VLESS Reality; a common site domain is recommended.
protocolPicker.subtitle: Node names are independent of VPS names — you can deploy multiple protocol instances on the same machine.
protocolPicker.tip1: Use distinct node names for different purposes, e.g. main line, backup line, UDP-only line.
protocolPicker.tip2: Use 443 or 8443 first for VLESS Reality; use high UDP ports for Hysteria2.
protocolPicker.tip3: If you change the protocol or port, update the cloud security group rules as well.
protocolPicker.title: Name the node and pick a protocol
protocolPicker.vlessFirewall: Allow the TCP port in cloud firewall / security groups
protocolPicker.vlessScenario: Mainstream clients and typical network environments — compatibility first
protocolPicker.vlessSubtitle: More universal — suits mainstream clients and regular TCP scenarios.
